name: Colombia
description: Colombia offers an increasingly attractive profile for expats, drawing them in with its affordable lifestyle, diverse climates, and genuinely warm culture. The country presents a unique blend of vibrant city life, stunning natural beauty, and a cost of living significantly lower than many Western nations.
longdescription: Expat life in Colombia is characterized by a high quality of life at a manageable cost. Cities like Medellín boast a year-round spring climate and a thriving expat community, while Bogotá offers a cosmopolitan atmosphere with rich cultural and culinary scenes. The economy is growing, with improving infrastructure, particularly in internet connectivity, making it appealing for digital nomads and remote workers. Colombian society is known for its warmth and family-centric culture, with locals generally welcoming to foreigners who make an effort to integrate. While safety concerns persist in some areas, major expat hubs are considered safe, and the country's reputation has significantly transformed over the past decades. Expats can enjoy a slower pace of life, access to world-class and affordable healthcare, and a vibrant social scene filled with music, dance, and festivals.

visas.name: Colombia Digital Nomad Visa
visas.description: Colombia's digital nomad visa (Nómada Digital) allows remote workers to live in Colombia for up to 2 years while working for foreign employers or clients.
benefits: 2-year renewable visa
Work legally as a remote worker
Path to residency
Affordable cost of living
Vibrant expat community
visas.path_to_residency_description: After 5 years of continuous legal residence, you may apply for permanent residency.
required_documents: Passport
Employment or client contract
Proof of monthly income ($3,000+)
Health insurance
Bank statements (3 months)
Police clearance

visas.name: Colombia Pensionado Visa
visas.description: Retirement visa for those receiving a pension or regular passive income of at least 3x the Colombian minimum wage (~$650/month).
benefits: Live in Colombia indefinitely
Renewable annually
Low cost of living
Warm climate year-round
Path to permanent residency
visas.path_to_residency_description: After 5 years as a visa holder, eligible to apply for permanent residency (Resident Visa).
required_documents: Passport
Proof of pension or passive income
Bank statements
Health insurance in Colombia
Police clearance

visas.name: Visa V – Nómadas Digitales (Digital Nomad Visa)
visas.description: The 'Visa V – Nómadas Digitales (Digital Nomad Visa)' in Colombia is a temporary residence permit for foreign citizens who wish to reside in the country while working remotely. It allows individuals to perform their professional activities for companies or clients located outside of Colombia, leveraging digital means.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are remote employees of foreign companies, freelancers providing services to international clients, or digital entrepreneurs running businesses registered abroad, all earning income from sources outside of Colombia.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Time spent on the Digital Nomad Visa (Visa V) does not count towards the time required to apply for permanent residency in Colombia. This visa is not a residency-track visa.
visas.renewal_conditions: Applicants can renew the visa if they continue to meet the established requirements, including the minimum income threshold and holding valid health insurance.
visas.tax_implications: Holders of the Digital Nomad Visa are generally not considered tax residents for their foreign income if they stay less than 183 days within a 12-month period. If an individual exceeds 183 days, they may become a tax resident and be subject to Colombian tax on their worldwide income.
benefits: Legal residency in Colombia for up to two years.
Permission to work remotely for non-Colombian employers or clients.
Eligibility to obtain a Cédula de Extranjería (foreigner ID card) for local services.
Multiple entries into and exits from Colombia while the visa is valid.
Opportunity to experience Colombian culture and environment without relying on short-term tourist visas.
required_documents: Valid passport with at least six months of validity remaining and blank pages
One digital photo (3x4 cm, white background, no accessories)
Copy of most recent entry stamp, tourist extension, or previous visa (if applicable)
Letter from foreign company/client or proof of digital entrepreneurship (in Spanish or English, or official translation)
Bank statements from the previous three months demonstrating required monthly income
Motivational letter (for entrepreneurs, describing digital project, financial resources, and intended stay)
Health insurance policy with coverage in Colombia for emergencies, accidents, hospitalization, and repatriation
Certificate of judicial, criminal, or police record from home country and/or places of residence in the last three years (not older than three months, apostilled/legalized if required)
application_process_steps: Gather all required documents and ensure they are translated to Spanish by an official translator if not originally in Spanish.
Complete the online visa application form through the official Cancillería de Colombia portal (SITAC).
Upload all necessary documents in digital format.
Pay the non-refundable study fee (Tarifa de Estudio).
Wait for the application review and decision (typically 15-30 days).
If approved, pay the visa issuance fee (Tarifa de Expedición).
Enter Colombia (if applying from abroad) and complete local registration to obtain the Cédula de Extranjería.

visas.name: M-Pensionado (Retirement Visa)
visas.description: The M-Pensionado visa, governed by Resolution 5477 of 2022, is a 3-year residency visa for foreign retirees seeking to live in Colombia. It allows individuals with a verifiable monthly pension to reside in the country and offers a pathway to permanent residency and eventually Colombian citizenship.
visas.target_applicant: Retired individuals receiving a stable, lifetime monthly pension from a government or private fund, who wish to reside in Colombia without working.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After holding the M-Pensionado visa for five continuous years, applicants are eligible to apply for a Resident (R) visa, which grants permanent residency. After five years on the R visa (total 10 years of legal residency), individuals can apply for Colombian citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must maintain the required pension income threshold and physically reside in Colombia for at least 180 days per year. The visa loses validity if the holder stays outside Colombia for more than 6 continuous months.
visas.tax_implications: Foreign-sourced pensions below 1,000 UVT (Unidad de Valor Tributario) per month are exempt from Colombian income tax. However, individuals residing in Colombia for more than 183 days become tax residents and may be subject to Colombian tax rules on other income. U.S. citizens remain liable for U.S. taxes on their worldwide income.
benefits: Full Colombian residency and a foreign resident ID (Cédula de Extranjería) allowing unrestricted stay.
Clear pathway to permanent residency (R visa) after 5 years and potential citizenship.
Ability to include spouse, registered domestic partner, and dependent children under 25 (or disabled children of any age) on dependent visas.
Access to Colombia's healthcare system and a lower cost of living compared to many Western nations.
Foreign-sourced pensions below a certain threshold are exempt from Colombian income tax.
required_documents: Valid passport with at least 6 months validity and two blank pages.
Official pension certificate stating a lifetime monthly pension not less than three times the Colombian monthly minimum wage, apostilled/legalized and officially translated to Spanish.
Criminal background check from the country of origin and any country resided in for the last three years, apostilled/legalized and officially translated to Spanish.
Psychophysical medical certificate (medical fitness certificate), apostilled/legalized and officially translated if issued abroad.
Proof of health insurance coverage in Colombia or a comprehensive health policy.
Recent digital photograph (3x4 cm, white background, no accessories, facing camera, neutral expression, ears uncovered).
Copy of latest entry stamp or previous visa/Cédula de Extranjería (if applicable).
application_process_steps: Gather and prepare all required documents, ensuring foreign documents are apostilled/legalized and translated to Spanish.
Complete and submit the online visa application form through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Cancillería) online portal.
Pay the application study fee online.
Await review and decision; processing typically takes 10 to 30 days.
Upon approval, pay the visa issuance fee and proceed to have the visa stamped in your passport (if applying abroad, at a consulate; if in Colombia, at Cancillería).
Register with Migración Colombia and obtain a Cédula de Extranjería (Foreign Resident ID) within 15 calendar days of visa issuance or entry.

visas.name: Rentista Visa (Passive Income Visa)
visas.description: The Rentista Visa (Visa V Rentista) is for foreign nationals who wish to reside in Colombia based on stable and recurring passive income from lawful sources, such as annuities, property rentals, dividends, or investment interest. This visa allows for temporary stay in the country without the need for local employment.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal for individuals with consistent passive income generated from abroad who intend to live in Colombia without engaging in local employment.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Rentista Visa is classified as a Visitor (V) Visa under Resolution 5477 of 2022 and does not accumulate time towards obtaining permanent residency in Colombia.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must continue to meet the income threshold and not remain outside Colombia for six or more consecutive months.
benefits: Grants temporary residency in Colombia.
Allows residing in Colombia without requiring employment.
Holders are eligible to apply for a Cédula de Extranjería (Foreign ID card).
Permits study in Colombia.
Allows multiple entries and exits from Colombia.
required_documents: Scan of the passport's biographical data page (valid for at least 6 months).
Digital passport-style photo (white background, max 100 KB, JPG format, no earrings, hats, or white shirts).
Cover letter explaining the passive income source and average monthly amount.
Certificate from a public or private entity or financial institution, recognized by the respective government, verifying a monthly income of at least 10 Colombian legal minimum wages.
Bank statements showing regular deposits of this income over the last 6 months.

Judicial, criminal, or police background check issued by the authority of the country where the applicant has resided for the last three (3) years, apostilled or legalized and translated into Spanish.
International health insurance policy covering the entire stay in Colombia, including accidents, illness, hospitalization, maternity, disability, and repatriation.
Proof of regular migratory status in the current country of residence (if applying from a country other than nationality).
Copies of previous Colombian visas (if applicable).
application_process_steps: Gather all required documents, ensuring they are apostilled/legalized and translated into Spanish if necessary.
Complete the online visa application form through the Colombian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Cancillería) website.
Upload all required documents and a digital passport-style photo.
Pay the non-refundable visa study fee (tasa administrativa de estudio).
Wait for the government's response and any requests for additional information.
If approved, pay the visa issuance fee (tasa administrativa de expedición) and receive the electronic visa.
If in Colombia, travel to Bogotá to have the visa stamped in the passport at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs office (if required).
Register the visa with Migración Colombia within 15 calendar days of approval to avoid penalties.

visas.name: Migrant Visa (Type M) - Work Visa
visas.description: The Migrant Visa (Type M) - Work Visa in Colombia is for foreign nationals who have secured an employment contract with a Colombian company and intend to reside and work in the country for a medium to long term. This visa allows the holder to legally live and work in Colombia for the duration of their contract, up to a maximum of three years, and serves as a pathway towards obtaining permanent residency.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are foreign professionals who have a formal job offer or contract for services from a legally registered company or natural person domiciled in Colombia.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Holding a Type M Work Visa accumulates time towards eligibility for a Type R (Resident) Visa. After residing continuously for five years in Colombia under a Migrant Visa, the holder can apply for permanent residency.
visas.renewal_conditions: The visa is renewable as long as the employment relationship with the sponsoring Colombian company continues. A new visa application is required if the employee changes employers.
benefits: Allows legal residence and work in Colombia for up to 3 years.
Renewable as long as the employment relationship continues.
Provides a path to permanent residency (Type R Visa) after accumulating 5 years of continuous residency under this visa type.
Permits the inclusion of dependents (spouse and minor children) on the same visa application.
Access to the Colombian Social Security System is required.
required_documents: Valid passport with at least six months of validity and sufficient space for the visa stamp.
Passport-style digital photograph (3x4 cm, color, white background, recent, head-on, JPG format, max 300 KB).
Online visa application form completed on the Cancillería website.
Employment contract or contract for services, duly signed, specifying activities, duration, and salary.
Letter of motivation from the employer detailing the applicant's functions, qualifications, reasons for hiring a foreign national, and the number of direct jobs generated by the company.
Certificate of existence and legal representation of the Colombian company, issued within the last three months, demonstrating its legal standing and tax registration (RUT).

Employer's bank statements for the last six months, demonstrating average monthly income of at least 100 times the legal monthly minimum wage (SMMLV) for a legal entity, or 10 SMMLV for a natural person.

Apostilled or legalized and officially translated professional credentials or academic degree (if applicable). For regulated professions, a permit or license from the competent Professional Council is required.
Criminal background check (apostilled or legalized and officially translated into Spanish if foreign).
Proof of health insurance with coverage in Colombia for the entire duration of the stay, valid for at least one year.
application_process_steps: Secure a formal employment contract or service agreement with a Colombian employer.
Gather all required documents, ensuring foreign documents are apostilled or legalized and officially translated into Spanish.
Complete the online visa application form on the Colombian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Cancillería) website and upload all scanned documents.
Pay the visa study fee online.
Await the application review by the Cancillería; additional documents or an interview may be requested.
If approved, pay the visa issuance fee and the visa will be electronically issued.
Upon arrival in Colombia or once the visa is issued, register with Migración Colombia and obtain the 'Cédula de Extranjería' (Foreigner ID card) within 15 calendar days.

visas.name: Work Visitor Visa (Type V)
visas.description: The Work Visitor Visa (Type V) in Colombia is designed for foreign nationals who wish to enter the country for temporary work-related activities without the intention of establishing permanent residency. This visa encompasses various subcategories, including those for temporary service providers to Colombian entities and digital nomads working remotely for foreign companies.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants include specialists providing temporary technical assistance to public or private entities in Colombia, or remote workers employed by foreign companies/clients who wish to reside in Colombia for up to two years.
visas.path_to_residency_description: While Type V visas are generally temporary, the Digital Nomad subcategory offers a path to residency. After two years of continuous legal stay on a Type V Digital Nomad visa, the holder may apply for a Type R Resident Visa.
visas.renewal_conditions: The Type V visa is not directly renewable in the sense of a simple extension; each application is treated as a new one. Applicants must continue to meet the requirements of the specific visa category. It is not intended for establishing permanent residency in Colombia, and prolonged consecutive use might lead to denial if a long-term stay is implied.
visas.tax_implications: For holders of the Digital Nomad visa, spending 183 days or more within any rolling 365-day period triggers Colombian tax residency, making worldwide income, including foreign remote salary, subject to Colombia's progressive income tax rates (0-39%). For other work visitor visas, income earned from work performed in Colombia would generally be subject to Colombian taxation.
benefits: Allows legal temporary stay in Colombia for work purposes.
Enables providing specialized technical assistance or remote work for foreign entities.
Permits multiple entries and exits during its validity.
For visas with validity over three months, allows obtaining a Colombian Cédula de Extranjería (foreigner ID card).
required_documents: Valid passport with at least six months of remaining validity and at least two blank pages.
Digital color photograph (3x4 cm, white background, JPG format, max 300KB).
Completed online visa application form.
Proof of payment for the visa study and issuance fees.
Health insurance with comprehensive coverage in Colombia for the entire planned stay.
Certificate of judicial, criminal, or police record from the country of origin/residence for the last three years, duly apostilled or legalized and translated (if applicable).
Bank certifications or statements demonstrating financial solvency for the applicant (e.g., for Digital Nomad: average monthly income of at least 3 SMLMV for the last 3 months).

Specific documents depending on the work activity (e.g., contract summary/form from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, employer's motivation letter, employer's bank statements for Temporary Service Provider; or letter/contract from foreign company for Digital Nomad).
Academic diplomas, professional qualifications, or certifications of work experience, apostilled or legalized and translated (if applicable).
application_process_steps: Complete the electronic visa application form available on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs website.
Scan and upload all required documents according to the specified format and size guidelines.
Pay the visa study fee (non-refundable) through the online platform or designated payment methods.
Await the evaluation and decision from the visa authority, which can take between 5 to 30 calendar days.
Upon approval, pay the visa issuance fee.

If the visa is granted for more than three months, register with Migración Colombia and obtain the Cédula de Extranjería (foreigner's ID card) within 15 days of arrival in Colombia or visa issuance (if already in the country).

visas.name: Type V Student Visa (M-9)
visas.description: The Type V Student Visa in Colombia is for foreign nationals admitted to an educational institution for in-person, virtual, or distance learning, including pre-school, primary, secondary, vocational training, technical, undergraduate, or postgraduate studies, as well as student internships and academic exchanges. It grants legal residence in Colombia for the duration of the approved academic program. This visa category superseded previous designations like the M-9 Student Visa after Resolution 5477 of 2022.
visas.target_applicant: Individuals accepted into a public or private educational institution in Colombia for an academic program or internship lasting longer than 180 days (6 months).
visas.path_to_residency_description: This is a Visitor (Type V) visa, and time spent on a Type V visa generally does not count towards the residency time requirements for obtaining a Resident (Type R) visa in Colombia.
visas.renewal_conditions: To renew, applicants must provide certification from the educational institution confirming continued enrollment, satisfactory attendance, and completion of the course/studies for which the previous visa was issued, along with maintaining valid insurance coverage.
visas.tax_implications: Holders of a Type V Student Visa may become Colombian tax residents if they spend more than 183 calendar days, continuously or intermittently, within any 365-day period in Colombia. If classified as a tax resident, worldwide income (including foreign-sourced income) will be subject to Colombian income tax, following a progressive tax system. Non-tax residents are generally only taxed on Colombian-sourced income.
benefits: Permits legal stay in Colombia for the entire duration of the academic program.
Allows postgraduate students to work part-time for up to 20 hours per week, upon registration with Migración Colombia and the Ministry of Labor.
Facilitates academic exchanges, internships, and study-related activities in Colombia.
Enables obtaining a 'cédula de extranjería' (foreigner ID card), opening Colombian bank accounts, and signing lease agreements.
Renewable if the study program extends beyond the initial visa validity period.
required_documents: Valid passport with at least 6 months validity beyond the intended stay and at least 2 blank pages.
Passport-style photo (3x4 cm, color, white background, recent, head-on, no accessories, JPG format, maximum 300KB).
Completed visa application form submitted online via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs website.

Original admission letter or enrollment certificate from a Colombian educational institution recognized by the Ministry of Education, indicating the program, level, and duration (must be notarized if required).

Proof of financial means to cover tuition and living expenses, such as bank statements from the last 3-6 months showing at least 10 times the Colombian Minimum Legal Monthly Wage (SMMLV) or a notarized letter of economic responsibility/sponsorship. (10 SMMLV for 2026 is COP 17,509,050).
Health insurance policy with national coverage for the entire duration of stay, covering accidents, illness, maternity, hospitalization, death, and repatriation.
Criminal background check or police clearance certificate from the applicant's country of origin, apostilled/legalized and translated into Spanish if requested.
For minors (under 18), notarized parental authorization and designation of a responsible person during their stay in Colombia.
For subsequent visa applications, certification from the educational institution of attendance and completion of the previous course/studies.
Copy of legal entry stamp to Colombia (if applying from within Colombia).
Copy of any previous Colombian visas (if applicable).
application_process_steps: Obtain an official acceptance or enrollment letter from a Colombian educational institution recognized by the Ministry of Education.
Gather all required supporting documents, ensuring they are apostilled/legalized and officially translated into Spanish if necessary.
Complete the online visa application form on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Cancillería) website.
Pay the non-refundable visa study fee (COP 68,800).
Submit the complete application and all digital documents through the online portal or at a Colombian consulate abroad/visa office in Bogotá.
Await the initial evaluation and respond to any requests for additional documentation or attend an interview if required by the Consular Office.
If the visa is approved, pay the visa issuance fee (COP 219,300).

Upon receiving the visa (electronically or stamped in passport), if arriving from abroad, register with Migración Colombia within 15 calendar days of entry to obtain the 'cédula de extranjería' (foreigner ID card).

visas.name: M-6 Visa – Inversionista (Business/Company Shares Investor Visa)
visas.description: The M-6 Visa, officially known as Visa M – Inversionista, is a temporary residence visa for foreign nationals who make a qualifying investment in a Colombian business or company. It allows investors to reside legally in Colombia for the duration of the visa while maintaining their investment, and the time spent on this visa counts towards eligibility for permanent residency.
visas.target_applicant: This visa is ideal for entrepreneurs, business owners, and foreign investors seeking temporary residency in Colombia by investing capital in a new or existing Colombian company or business venture.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After five continuous years of holding a Migrant (M) visa, including the M-6 Investor Visa, the holder is eligible to apply for a Resident (R) Visa in Colombia, which grants permanent residency.
visas.renewal_conditions: The applicant must demonstrate that the qualifying investment was maintained throughout the validity of the previous visa, and all original eligibility criteria continue to be met.
benefits: Legal temporary residency in Colombia for up to three years, renewable.
Ability to live, study, and work in Colombia without additional permits.
Pathway to permanent residency (R Visa) after five continuous years.
Opportunity to include spouse and minor children as beneficiaries.
Access to Colombia's growing economy and investor-friendly environment.
required_documents: Completed online visa application form.
Valid passport with at least six months of validity and at least two blank pages.
Passport-style digital photograph (3cm x 4cm, white background, max 300kb .jpg).
Certificate of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) registration from the Banco de la República (Colombia's Central Bank), confirming the investment in your name.
Documents accrediting the investment in a Colombian company (e.g., certificate from the Chamber of Commerce, share certificates, company incorporation documents, or capital contribution records).
Criminal record certificate from your country of origin or last residence, duly apostilled or legalized and translated into Spanish by an official translator.

Proof of health insurance coverage in Colombia for the duration of the visa, meeting minimum coverage requirements (e.g., medical expenses of at least 100 SMMLV, death coverage of 30 SMMLV, and repatriation of remains coverage of 35 SMMLV).
Bank statements for the three months prior to the visa application demonstrating economic solvency to remain in the country.
application_process_steps: Make and officially register the qualifying investment with the Banco de la República.
Gather all required documentation, ensuring foreign documents are apostilled/legalized and officially translated into Spanish.
Complete and submit the visa application online through the official platform of the Colombian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Cancillería).
Pay the visa study fee upon application submission.
If approved, pay the visa issuance fee.
Upon approval, register the visa with Migración Colombia and obtain a Cédula de Extranjería (foreigner's ID card) within 15 calendar days of entry or visa approval.

visas.name: M-10 Real Estate Investment Visa
visas.description: The M-10 Real Estate Investment Visa in Colombia is for foreign nationals who invest in real estate within the country. It grants legal temporary residency, allowing the holder to reside in Colombia and conduct investment-related activities connected to their property.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are foreign nationals seeking legal residency in Colombia through a significant real estate investment, who wish to reside in the country and potentially gain permanent residency in the future.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After holding the M-10 Migrant Visa for five (5) consecutive years, applicants become eligible to apply for the Colombian Resident (R) Visa, which grants permanent residency status.
visas.renewal_conditions: The investment or property must be maintained throughout the validity of the previous visa, and the property's value must meet or exceed the updated minimum investment threshold (350 SMMLV) at the time of renewal.
visas.tax_implications: Foreign investors are subject to Colombian tax obligations on income generated from Colombian sources, including rental income and capital gains. Colombia has double taxation agreements with various countries. Tax considerations include wealth tax, annual property tax, and reporting obligations which vary based on tax residency status.
benefits: Legally reside in Colombia for the duration of the visa
Own and maintain real estate as a foreign national
Enter and exit the country freely while the visa is valid
Accumulate continuous residency time towards permanent residency
Ability to include spouse and minor children as beneficiaries
required_documents: Valid passport copy (bio-page and relevant visa stamps)
Certificado de Tradición y Libertad del inmueble (property's legal history document, issued no more than 30-90 days before application)
Escritura Pública de compraventa registrada (public deed of sale)
Comunicación expedida por el Departamento de Cambios Internacionales del Banco de la República (Formulario 4) confirming registration of foreign direct investment for real estate purchase
Proof of economic solvency to remain in the country (e.g., bank statements for the last three months)
Private health insurance valid in Colombia for the duration of the visa
Criminal background check (apostilled if issued abroad)
Passport-style face photo (3cm x 4cm, white background)
Movementos Migratorios (migratory movements certificate)
application_process_steps: Complete the real estate investment and ensure funds are registered as Foreign Direct Investment with the Banco de la República (Formulario 4)
Gather all required documents, ensuring foreign documents are apostilled and then translated by an official translator in Colombia
Submit the online visa application through the Colombian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Cancillería) website
Undergo application review, which may include requests for additional documentation or interviews
Receive visa approval and issuance
Register the visa with Migración Colombia upon arrival in the country to obtain a 'cédula de extranjería' (foreigners ID card)

visas.name: Migrant Visa Investor (Foreign Direct Investment - FDI)
visas.description: The Migrant Visa Investor (Type M) in Colombia is designed for foreign nationals who make a significant direct foreign investment in the country, either through a company, business, or by acquiring real estate. It allows investors to reside legally in Colombia, manage their investments, and provides a pathway to permanent residency.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are entrepreneurs, business owners, or individuals looking to invest foreign capital in Colombian companies, businesses, or real estate, seeking long-term residency.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After five continuous years of holding the Migrant (M) Investor Visa and maintaining the investment, applicants become eligible to apply for the Resident (R) Visa, which grants permanent residency. A higher investment amount (currently 650 SMMLV) may qualify for direct application to the Resident (R) Visa. [cite: 4, 7 (from a previous turn), 9 (from a previous turn)]
visas.renewal_conditions: The applicant must demonstrate that the investment or property ownership was maintained throughout the validity of the previous visa. [cite: 5 (from a previous turn), 11 (from a previous turn), 13 (from a previous turn)]
benefits: Legal residency in Colombia for up to three years.
Ability to work in Colombia, specifically within the invested company or generally under the investor visa.
Accumulates time towards obtaining permanent residency.
Allows for family reunification by enabling dependents to apply for beneficiary visas. [cite: 6 (from a previous turn)]
Access to Colombia's health system and other social benefits as a resident.
required_documents: Valid passport with at least two blank pages and minimum 6 months validity. [cite: 3 (from a previous turn)]
Digital passport-style photo (3x4 cm, white background, no accessories, JPG format, max 300 KB). [cite: 3 (from a previous turn)]

Proof of foreign direct investment registration with the Banco de la República (Central Bank), such as a communication or certificate from the International Exchange Department. [cite: 4 (from a previous turn), 5 (from a previous turn)]

Document proving the investment (e.g., public deed for real estate, certificate of company shares from the Chamber of Commerce, or capital contribution records). [cite: 4 (from a previous turn), 5 (from a previous turn)]

For real estate: Updated Certificate of Tradition and Liberty (Certificado de Tradición y Libertad) showing exclusive ownership by the applicant. [cite: 4 (from a previous turn), 5 (from a previous turn)]
Bank statements from the last three months demonstrating sufficient economic solvency to remain in Colombia. [cite: 5 (from a previous turn)]
Criminal background check from country of origin, apostilled or legalized and officially translated into Spanish. [cite: 8 (from a previous turn)]
Proof of health coverage in Colombia or a health insurance policy with nationwide coverage. [cite: 6 (from a previous turn), 9 (from a previous turn)]
Copy of last entry/exit stamps for Colombia or previous Colombian visas, if applicable. [cite: 3 (from a previous turn)]
application_process_steps: Make a qualifying investment in Colombia and ensure it is properly registered as foreign direct investment with the Banco de la República. [cite: 4 (from a previous turn), 5]
Gather all required documentation, ensuring foreign documents are apostilled/legalized and translated into Spanish if necessary. [cite: 4 (from a previous turn), 5 (from a previous turn)]
Submit the visa application online through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' official platform (Cancillería de Colombia).
Pay the non-refundable study fee.
Respond to any requests for additional information from the visa authority.
Upon approval, pay the visa issuance fee within the stipulated timeframe.

visas.name: Spouse & Partner Visa (Type M)
visas.description: The Colombia Spouse & Partner Visa (Type M) is for foreign nationals who are legally married to or in a recognized permanent union with a Colombian citizen, and wish to reside in Colombia. This visa allows for legal temporary residency in the country and grants the holder the right to engage in any legal economic activity.
visas.target_applicant: Foreigners legally married to a Colombian citizen or who have a recognized permanent union (unión marital de hecho) with a Colombian citizen, intending to live together in Colombia.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Holders of the Type M Spouse Visa can apply for a Resident Visa (Type R) after 2-3 years of continuous and uninterrupted holding of the Type M visa if married, or after 5 years if in a permanent union (unión marital de hecho).
visas.renewal_conditions: The marriage or permanent union must remain valid and the applicant must continue to meet all required conditions set forth by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
benefits: Open work permit, allowing engagement in any legal activity without employer restrictions.
Fastest path to Colombian permanent residency, qualifying after 2-3 years for married couples or 5 years for permanent partners.
Both legal marriage and permanent civil unions (unión marital de hecho) are officially recognized for this visa category.
Access to the Colombian Social Security System.
Family stability and recognized legal grounds for stay.
required_documents: Valid passport of the foreign applicant with at least two blank pages and minimum 6 months validity.
Digital passport-style photograph (3x4 cm, white background, no accessories, front-facing, both eyes open, ears visible).

Authentic copy of the Colombian Civil Marriage Certificate or Public Deed of Permanent Union, issued no more than 3 months prior to the application, apostilled or legalized and officially translated into Spanish if issued abroad.
Copy of the Colombian spouse/partner's national ID (cédula de ciudadanía).
Criminal background check from the applicant's country of origin, apostilled or legalized and officially translated into Spanish.

Proof of current shared life (e.g., joint lease, shared bank account statements, photos with dates, airline tickets/hotel reservations from trips as a couple, joint contracts, screenshots of conversations, sworn statement of cohabitation).

Letter of request signed by the Colombian spouse/partner, stating effective cohabitation, commitment to inform immigration of changes, and including their contact details (address, email, phone), with an authenticated signature.
Certificate of Migratory Movements for both the foreign applicant and the Colombian spouse/partner, issued by Migración Colombia.
Special Power of Attorney from the Colombian spouse/partner authorizing the foreign applicant to process the visa, duly authenticated.
Copy of the most recent entry stamp, tourist extension, or previous Colombian visa (if applicable).
Health policy providing extensive coverage for all-risk (accident, illness, maternity, disability, hospitalization), death, and repatriation.
application_process_steps: Gather and prepare all required documents, ensuring they are apostilled/legalized and officially translated into Spanish where necessary.
Complete the online visa application form through the Cancillería de Colombia's official website.
Pay the non-refundable visa study fee (COP 232,200).
Await the government's decision; the processing time is typically 15-30 calendar days, though additional information requests may extend this.
Upon approval, pay the visa issuance fee (COP 1,161,000) and receive the electronic visa.

Upon entering Colombia (or if already in Colombia), apply for the Cédula de Extranjería (foreigner's ID card) and complete the registration with Migración Colombia within 15 calendar days of visa issuance or entry.

visas.name: Parent of a Colombian National Visa (Type M)
visas.description: This visa is for foreign fathers and mothers of Colombian citizen children, allowing them to legally reside in Colombia with their child. It grants an open work permit and is a pathway towards permanent residency.
visas.target_applicant: Foreign parents (biological or adoptive) of a Colombian national by birth who wish to live permanently in Colombia with their child.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After two continuous years as a holder of the Type M Parent of a Colombian National Visa, the applicant may apply for the Colombian Resident Visa (Type R), which grants permanent residency.
visas.renewal_conditions: The parent-child relationship must continue, and the applicant must comply with all immigration regulations.
benefits: Family reunification with a Colombian child is protected by Colombian immigration law.
Grants an open work permit, allowing the holder to work freely in any legal activity in Colombia without employer restrictions.
Valid for up to 3 years and is renewable as long as the parent-child relationship continues.
Accumulates time towards obtaining the Colombian Resident Visa (Type R) after 2 years.
Allows access to the Colombian social security system and a foreign identification card (cédula de extranjería).
required_documents: Authentic and recent copy of the Colombian birth certificate of the child (usually no more than 3 months old). If both parents are foreigners, the certificate must include an annotation indicating its validity for demonstrating nationality and be available in the Registry Entity's database.

Visa application letter: If the Colombian child is a minor, the letter must be signed by the other parent, stating that the foreign parent is fulfilling all child support obligations. If both parents are foreigners, both must sign. If the Colombian child is of legal age, they must present a handwritten letter with a fingerprint (index or thumb) requesting the visa for their foreign parent, accompanied by a copy of their Colombian ID (Cédula de Ciudadanía).
Valid passport in good condition with available pages, with a minimum validity of six months at the time of application (exceptions for Venezuelan citizens with expired passports).
Proof of economic solvency: Bank statements from the last 6 months showing average balances and sources of income to demonstrate sufficient financial resources to support oneself in Colombia.
Certificate of Migratory Movements issued by Migración Colombia, dated within three months of the visa application, to accredit the movements of both parents.
Previous visa documentation: The foreign parent must provide a copy of the visa they held at the time of the minor's birth that granted domicile (if applicable).
application_process_steps: Gather all required documents, ensuring they are authentic, recent, translated (if necessary), and apostilled/legalized.
Complete the online visa application form (DS-160 Migratorio Colombiano) through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' visa portal.
Pay the visa study fee (USD 54.92 as of 2026).
Submit the application and all supporting documents online.
If approved, pay the visa expedition fee (USD 270.40 as of 2026).
Once the visa is stamped in the passport, apply for the 'Cédula de Extranjería' at a Migración Colombia office.

visas.name: Beneficiary Visa (for Dependents)
visas.description: The Beneficiary Visa in Colombia is for immediate family members who are economically dependent on a foreigner holding a principal visa (Migrant 'M', Resident 'R', or specific Visitor 'V' visas) in Colombia. This visa allows eligible dependents to reside in Colombia with the principal visa holder, but it does not grant permission to work.
visas.target_applicant: Spouses or permanent partners, and children under 25 years of age (or older children with certified disabilities preventing economic independence) who are financially dependent on a primary visa holder in Colombia.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After five continuous years of holding a Beneficiary Visa, the applicant may be eligible to apply for a Resident (Type R) visa in Colombia.
visas.renewal_conditions: The beneficiary visa can be renewed as long as the marital/family relationship with the principal visa holder remains valid and the principal visa holder maintains their visa status. The visa automatically expires when a child beneficiary turns 25 or ceases to be economically dependent.
benefits: Allows legal residency in Colombia for the duration of the principal visa.
Provides immigration stability for family members.
Permits multiple entries and exits from Colombia.
Offers a path to a Resident visa after five continuous years of holding the beneficiary visa.
Allows for activities such as studying, signing contracts, and opening bank accounts (excluding work).
required_documents: Photo (passport-style, 3x4 cm, white background, JPG, max 300kb).
Photocopy of the main page of the applicant's passport with at least 6 months validity.
Photocopy of the passport page with the last entry/exit stamp for Colombia, or extension of stay/safe passage (if applying from within Colombia).
Copy of the current visa and 'cedula de extranjeria' (foreign ID) of the principal visa holder.

Authentic copy of marriage certificate, birth certificate, or other document proving the relationship or family link with the principal visa holder. If foreign, it must be apostilled/legalized and officially translated into Spanish.

Written communication signed by the principal visa holder requesting the beneficiary visa and declaring economic dependence and responsibility for the beneficiary's expenses, including health coverage.

Proof of financial responsibility from the principal visa holder, demonstrated through bank statements for the last 6 months or an employment certification, showing sufficient income to support the beneficiary.
Health insurance with coverage in Colombia for each beneficiary (accidents, death, hospitalization, repatriation).
Criminal background check certificate from the country of residence for the last three years (apostilled/legalized and translated).
application_process_steps: Gather and prepare all required documentation, ensuring foreign documents are apostilled/legalized and translated into Spanish.
Complete the online visa application form on the official Ministry of Foreign Affairs website and upload scanned documents and photo.
Pay the visa study (application review) fee.
Await the visa application review and respond to any additional government requests.
If approved, pay the visa issuance fee (amount varies based on the principal visa type).
If in Colombia, travel to Bogotá to have the visa stamped in the passport (if not issued electronically), and then coordinate an appointment to obtain the 'cedula de extranjeria' (foreign ID card).

visas.name: Independent Professional Visa (Type M)
visas.description: The 'Independent Professional Visa (Type M)' in Colombia is for foreign nationals who wish to reside and practice their profession or engage in professional activities independently within the country. It allows the holder to legally exercise their profession, whether regulated or, exceptionally, a non-regulated activity deemed of interest to Colombia.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a professional with recognized qualifications or exceptional skills who intends to work in Colombia as a self-employed individual in their specific field.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After five years as a holder of the Type M visa, the applicant can apply for a Resident Visa.
visas.renewal_conditions: The visa can be renewed as long as the holder continues to meet the requirements for practicing their profession or activity and maintains compliance with Colombian laws.
visas.tax_implications: Holders of the Type M visa are considered residents in Colombia for tax purposes.
benefits: Allows legal exercise of a specific profession or activity in Colombia.
Provides a path to permanent residency after five years as a visa holder.
Permits the inclusion of dependents (spouse, permanent partner, and children).
Eligible to apply for the 'Cédula de Extranjería' (foreigner ID card).
Considered a resident for tax purposes.
required_documents: Valid passport with at least six months of validity.
Two 3x4 cm passport-style photos with white background.
Online visa application form completed.
Letter describing the profession or activity to be performed in Colombia.
Copy of professional degree validation from the Ministry of Education or relevant authority.
Proof of compliance with other requirements for practicing the profession, such as a professional card, license, or provisional permit (if regulated).
Bank certification showing an average monthly income equal to or greater than five legal monthly minimum wages for the last six months (approximately COP 5,800,000 in 2023).
Proof of health coverage in Colombia or an international health insurance policy covering the stay.
Certificates or documents supporting suitability and professional experience (for activities based on experience rather than academic training).
application_process_steps: Complete the online visa application form through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs portal.
Gather and prepare all required documents, ensuring professional qualifications are validated and financial statements are current.
Submit the application and pay the study fee.
Respond to any additional requirements from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
If approved, pay the visa expedition fee.
Once the visa is approved, register with Migración Colombia and apply for the 'Cédula de Extranjería' within 15 days.

visas.name: Resident Visa (Type R)
visas.description: The Resident Visa (Type R) is Colombia's permanent residency visa, allowing foreigners to live, work, and pursue any legal activity in the country indefinitely. It represents the highest level of immigration stability and is the final step before applying for Colombian nationality by adoption.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are foreigners who have accumulated a required period of continuous residency under a Migrant (Type M) visa, have close family ties to Colombian citizens, or have made a significant direct foreign investment in Colombia.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Resident Visa (Type R) is, by definition, permanent residency. It is the final step before applying for Colombian nationality (citizenship) by adoption. Depending on the case, one can apply for citizenship after 2 or 5 years of holding the Type R visa.
visas.renewal_conditions: The visa is valid for 5 years and requires a 'visa transfer' (traspaso de visa) every five years to a new passport or document; this is an administrative step, not a new application. Failure to complete this transfer can result in loss of permanent residency status. The holder must not remain outside Colombia for more than two consecutive years, or the visa may be revoked.
benefits: Indefinite residency in Colombia.
Full work freedom to pursue any legal activity without being tied to a specific employment contract or company.
Ability to include dependent family members (spouse/permanent partner, and children under 25 years demonstrating financial dependence).
Direct pathway to Colombian nationality by adoption.
Access to the national healthcare system and insurance program.
required_documents: Valid passport with sufficient space for a new visa stamp.
Migration movements certificate from Migración Colombia, proving uninterrupted stay in the country.
Criminal background check from country of origin and any country lived in for the past 5 years.
Passport-style photo meeting Cancillería de Colombia specifications.
Copies of all previous Type M visa resolutions (if applying by accumulated time).

Specific documents proving the qualifying category (e.g., proof of foreign direct investment, marriage certificate for spouse of Colombian national, birth certificate for parent of Colombian national, proof of pension benefits).
Proof of international health insurance covering all medical risks including repatriation of remains.
All foreign documents must be apostilled or consularly legalized and officially translated into Spanish.
application_process_steps: Determine eligibility based on qualifying categories (e.g., accumulated time on an M visa, family ties, or direct investment).
Gather all required documents, ensuring they are apostilled/legalized and officially translated into Spanish where necessary.
Complete the online application through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Cancillería) official platform (visa.cancilleria.gov.co).
Pay the non-refundable study fee (approximately USD 55-56).
Wait for the visa application review, which can take up to 30 calendar days.
If approved, pay the issuance fee (approximately USD 232-280) within the defined deadline.
Download the electronic visa PDF.
Register with Migración Colombia and obtain/update the 'Cédula de Extranjería' (foreigner ID card) within 15 calendar days of visa issuance or entry into Colombia.

visas.name: Andean Migrant Visa (Type M)
visas.description: The Andean Migrant Visa (Type M) allows citizens of Bolivia, Ecuador, and Peru to reside and work legally in Colombia. It serves as a pathway for temporary residence for individuals seeking to establish themselves in the country for a period longer than a visitor's stay, and can lead to permanent residency.
visas.target_applicant: Citizens of Bolivia, Ecuador, or Peru who intend to live and work in Colombia and establish temporary residence.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After holding the Type M Andean Migrant Visa for two continuous years, applicants are eligible to apply for a Type R (Resident) Visa, which grants permanent residency in Colombia. The application for the Resident Visa must be submitted within 90 days before the expiration of the Type M visa.
visas.renewal_conditions: The Andean Migrant Visa (Type M) is granted only once for up to two years. After this period, the holder may apply for a Resident Visa (Type R) by accumulation of time, provided they have maintained continuous residence.
benefits: Open work permit, allowing the holder to undertake any legal activity without employer sponsorship.
Ability to include immediate family members (spouse/permanent partner and dependent children under 25) as beneficiaries.
Access to financial services, such as opening bank accounts and obtaining credit.
Opportunity to join the Colombian health system (EPS).
Accumulates time towards qualifying for a Resident Visa (Type R) after two years.
required_documents: Valid passport with a minimum validity of six months and at least two blank pages.

Digital color photograph with a white background (4x3 cm, facing forward, head centered, eyes open, ears visible, no glare, hair or accessories covering face, JPG format, max 300 KB, recent and different from previous visas/passport).
Copy of the last entry/exit stamp or migratory card if applying from within Colombia.

Certificate of judicial, criminal, or police records from the country of nationality or countries of residence for the last three to five years, apostilled or legalized and officially translated to Spanish.
Written statement (motivation letter) explaining the purpose of establishing temporary residence in Colombia and detailing the means of subsistence for the stay.
Proof of legal residency in an Andean Community country for at least one year before the application (if applicable).
Cédula de identidad del país de origen (Identity card from country of origin).
International health insurance with broad coverage (accident, illness, maternity, disability, hospitalization, death, and repatriation).
application_process_steps: Gather all required documents, ensuring they are apostilled/legalized and translated to Spanish where necessary.
Complete the online visa application form on the Cancillería's website.
Pay the visa study fee (Tasa Administrativa de Estudio) online.
Submit the application and supporting documents electronically.
Await the government's response and any additional requirements (the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has 30 calendar days to process the application).
If approved, pay the visa expedition fee (Tasa Administrativa de Expedición).
Receive the electronic visa and follow instructions for obtaining the 'Cédula de Extranjería' (foreign identification card) from Migración Colombia.

visas.name: Resident by Temporary Protection Status (Venezuelan Migrants) (Type R)
visas.description: This Resident by Temporary Protection Status (Type R) visa is a specific pathway to permanent residency in Colombia for Venezuelan migrants who have consistently held legal status under the Estatuto Temporal de Protección para Migrantes Venezolanos (ETPV) for a minimum of five years. It allows beneficiaries to transition from temporary protection to a stable, long-term migratory status.
visas.target_applicant: Venezuelan migrants who have accumulated five continuous and uninterrupted years of legal stay in Colombia through the Permiso Especial de Permanencia (PEP) or Permiso por Protección Temporal (PPT) under the ETPV framework.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This Type R visa *is* the permanent residency status for eligible Venezuelan migrants. It allows beneficiaries of the ETPV who have completed 5 years of legal stay to formalize their migratory status as permanent residents in Colombia.
visas.renewal_conditions: The Permanent Resident (R) visa automatically loses its validity if the holder is absent from Colombian territory for two consecutive uninterrupted years.
benefits: Grants permanent legal residency in Colombia.
Allows the holder to live and work legally in Colombia without restrictions on activity type.
Provides a stable and long-term migratory status in the country.
required_documents: Valid Venezuelan passport (even expired passports are accepted for those who entered regularly, as per Resolution 2231 of June 9, 2021).

All Permiso por Protección Temporal (PPT) and/or Permiso Especial de Permanencia (PEP) documents covering the full 5-year ETPV period, in correct chronological order, demonstrating continuous and uninterrupted legal stay.
Current PPT must be valid at the time of application.
Certificate of Migration Movements (Certificado de Movimientos Migratorios) from Migración Colombia for the last six years.
Criminal background certificate from Venezuela, apostilled and officially translated into Spanish.
Proof of economic solvency or regular income demonstrating capacity to support oneself in Colombia.
Passport-style photograph meeting Cancillería de Colombia specifications.
application_process_steps: Verify eligibility by confirming 5 continuous and uninterrupted years of legal stay under PEP and/or PPT within the ETPV framework.
Ensure the current Permiso por Protección Temporal (PPT) is valid.
Gather all required documents, including passport, previous migration permits, migration movements certificate, criminal background check, proof of economic solvency, and a passport-style photo.
Submit the visa application through the official website of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Cancillería de Colombia).
If approved, pay the visa expedition fee.
Register the approved visa with Migración Colombia to obtain the Cédula de Extranjería (Foreign ID).

visas.name: Permanent Correspondent Visa (Type V)
visas.description: This visa is designed for foreign nationals employed by foreign media organizations to work as permanent press correspondents in Colombia. It allows the holder to reside in Colombia and conduct journalistic activities on behalf of their employer, such as covering local news, reporting on current events, and serving as a correspondent for their media organization.
visas.target_applicant: Journalists, photographers, and other media professionals who need to be based in Colombia for extended periods to fulfill their professional duties for international media outlets.
visas.renewal_conditions: The applicant must continue to meet the initial criteria and remain employed by the foreign media outlet.
benefits: Allows foreign journalists to legally reside in Colombia and work as permanent correspondents for international media outlets.
Provides flexibility for media professionals to enter and exit the country as needed to cover stories and news events.
Enables journalists to stay for an extended period, contributing to in-depth coverage of local and regional news.
required_documents: Letter from the legal representative of the foreign media organization, including full identification of media, contact details, complete identification of the foreign journalist, detailed explanation of journalistic activities in Colombia, explanation of the relationship and the journalist's special qualifications (if applicable), and a declaration of financial responsibility for the correspondent's travel and stay expenses in Colombia.
Proof of financial liquidity (6 months of bank statements) for both the media organization and the applicant.
Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation for foreign private media companies, duly apostilled or legalized, along with an official translation into Spanish (if necessary).
Proof of journalist or press correspondent status.
Valid passport with a minimum validity of six (6) months.
Digital photograph (3x4 cm, white background, JPEG format, maximum 300KB).
Online application form completed through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs website.
International health insurance with full coverage in Colombia, including accidents, illness, maternity, hospitalization, and repatriation.
Certificate of criminal/judicial background issued by the authority of the country where the applicant has resided during the last three (3) years.
application_process_steps: Gather all required documents, ensuring foreign documents are apostilled/legalized and officially translated into Spanish.
Fill out the electronic visa application form on the website of the Colombian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Cancillería).
Upload the digital photograph and all required documents in PDF format to the online system.
Pay the non-refundable application study fee.
Await review and decision from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Cancillería).
If the visa is approved, pay the visa expedition fee and have the visa stamped in your passport.

visas.name: Seasonal Agricultural Worker Visa (Type V)
visas.description: This visa is for foreign nationals who wish to perform seasonal agricultural work in Colombia under programs established by the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development or regional governments. It is a Visitor Visa (Type V) category designed for short-term stays, allowing legal employment in specific agricultural activities.
visas.target_applicant: Foreigners hired by a Colombian entity to undertake seasonal agricultural work.
benefits: Allows legal employment in specific seasonal agricultural activities in Colombia.
Provides a clear legal framework for temporary agricultural workers.
required_documents: Completed online visa application form from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs website.
Valid passport with a minimum of six months validity remaining and at least two blank pages.
A recent digital passport-style photograph in color with a white background and neutral expression (JPG format).
Written communication from the employer (Colombian agricultural company or organization) detailing the applicant's suitability for the agricultural work, specific tasks, and the length of employment.
Medical certificate issued by health authorities in the applicant's country of origin, certifying psychophysical aptitude for agricultural work.
Health insurance policy with coverage throughout the Colombian national territory.
Certificate of judicial, criminal, or police record from the applicant's country of origin or last country of residence.

Bank certification/statements from the employer for the six months prior to the application, demonstrating an average monthly income of no less than 100 legal monthly minimum wages (SMLMV) if the employer is a legal entity.
Employer's motivation letter explaining the need for the foreign worker.
Employment contract or a summary of the contract, specifying the start and end dates.
Certificate of existence and legal representation of the contracting company, issued no more than three months prior to the application.
application_process_steps: Gather and, if required, apostille or legalize all necessary documents.
Complete the online visa application form through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Cancillería) official website.
Pay the non-refundable visa study fee (if applicable).
Submit all required documentation electronically through the visa portal.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs reviews the application and may request additional information.
If approved, pay the visa issuance fee and obtain the visa.
Upon entry to Colombia or after visa issuance, apply for the 'Cédula de Extranjería' (foreigner ID card) with Migración Colombia within 15 calendar days.

extra_info:
### Visas & Notes
- Digital Nomad Visa (Digital Nomad Visa): 2-year renewable visa
- Pensionado visa for retirees with passive income
- Investor visa (Inversionista) for business owners

Citizenship by Descent.desc: Any person born outside Colombia to at least one Colombian parent (by birth or naturalization) is eligible for Colombian citizenship by descent. There is no residency, Spanish proficiency, or civics test requirement for this pathway. The Colombian parent must have held Colombian citizenship at the time of the child's birth. The process involves registering the birth at a Colombian consulate or at the Registraduría Nacional upon arrival in Colombia.

Naturalization.desc: Foreign nationals can apply for Colombian citizenship through naturalization after meeting specific residency requirements. The general requirement is five continuous years of legal residence in Colombia (with a valid resident visa). This period may be reduced to two years for those married to a Colombian citizen or one year for nationals of Latin American and Caribbean countries. Applicants must demonstrate good conduct, financial stability, and proficiency in Spanish, usually through a language and civics test, though those with a bachelor's degree from a Colombian university or over 65 years old may be exempt from tests.

Birthright.desc: Citizenship by birth (jus soli) is granted to anyone born in Colombia if at least one parent is a Colombian citizen or a foreign legal resident at the time of birth. Children born in Colombia to two foreign tourists or visitors without legal residency do not automatically qualify under jus soli alone. Children born to stateless parents in Colombia do qualify for Colombian citizenship to prevent statelessness.

Spouse and Family.desc: Foreigners married to Colombian citizens can apply for citizenship after two years of continuous legal residence, provided they hold an R-type resident visa. The process typically involves holding a Migrant (M) visa as a spouse for three years before becoming eligible for a Resident (R) visa, and then two years with the R visa before applying for citizenship. Proof of legal marriage recognized in Colombia and cohabitation is required.

tax_advice:
*   **Personal Income Tax:** Colombia operates a progressive personal income tax system with rates ranging from 0% to 39%. For the first five years of residency (183+ days per year), residents are generally taxed on a territorial basis (income earned within Colombia). After five years of qualifying residency, individuals are subject to worldwide taxation. Non-residents are taxed at a flat 35% on Colombian-source income.
*   **Corporate Tax:** The general corporate income tax (CIT) rate in Colombia is 35% for resident companies on their worldwide income. Certain sectors may face surcharges, such as financial institutions (additional 5% through 2027, making it 40%) and crude oil/coal extraction (5-15% surtax). Companies in free trade zones may enjoy a reduced rate of 20% on export-derived income.
*   **Value Added Tax (VAT):** The general VAT rate (Impuesto al Valor Agregado - IVA) in Colombia is 19%. However, some goods and services are subject to reduced rates of 5% or 0%, or are exempt.
*   **Capital Gains Tax:** Capital gains are generally taxed at a flat rate of 15% for assets held for two or more years. Gains from lotteries, gambling, or similar activities are taxed at 20%.
*   **Wealth Tax:** For individuals, a wealth tax may apply if net worth on January 1st exceeds certain thresholds. For the 2025 tax year, the threshold is 72,000 UVT, with progressive rates from 0.5% to 1.5%. For the fiscal year 2026, the Colombian government has proposed a reduction in the threshold to 40,000 UVT and an increase in rates up to 5%, which is currently under review by the Constitutional Court.
local_tips:
*   **Cost of Living:** Colombia is significantly more affordable than many Western countries, with monthly expenses for a comfortable single person ranging from approximately $1,800 to $2,500 USD in central neighborhoods of major cities like Medellín or Bogotá, excluding rent. A more modest lifestyle can be achieved on $1,000-$1,400 per month. Rent is a major variable, with 1-bedroom apartments in expat-popular areas of Medellín ranging from $700-$1,200/month, and similar prices in Bogotá ($600-$1,000 in Chapinero, $900-$1,500 in Usaquén/Zona G).
*   **Language:** Spanish is the official language. While English is spoken in tourist-heavy areas and high-end establishments, learning basic Spanish is highly recommended for daily life and cultural integration. Colombian Spanish is known for its clarity, especially in Bogotá, but regional accents and slang vary.
*   **Safety:** While Colombia's safety has improved dramatically, expats should remain aware of their surroundings and choose neighborhoods carefully. Major expat areas in cities like Medellín (El Poblado, Laureles) and Bogotá (Usaquén, Chico, Rosales) are generally considered safe and walkable.
*   **Registration:** Expats typically require a visa, such as the Digital Nomad Visa, Work Visa, or Pensionado Visa, to reside legally. After obtaining residency, foreigners can apply for a cédula (national ID card). Health insurance is mandatory for visa holders, with minimum coverage requirements.
